title: Records
cards/0/title: A value type in one line
cards/0/body: A record (C# 9) is a class for which the compiler writes the constructor, properties, content-based equality, ToString and deconstruction for you.
cards/1/q: a and b are two different record Point(1, 2) objects. What does a == b return?
cards/1/explain: A regular class would give False — it would compare references.
cards/2/body: The properties of a positional record are init: they don't change after creation. Need a modified version? Make a copy.
cards/2/code: var moved = a with { X = 10 };   // Point { X = 10, Y = 2 }, a is unchanged
cards/3/explain: Age is an init property. You change it with with.
cards/4/body: Since C# 10 there is record struct — a value type with the same conveniences. Its properties are mutable by default; readonly record struct makes them init.
cards/5/q: What does a record generate for you? Select all.
cards/5/options/1: A ToString that shows the contents
cards/5/explain: Saving is the ORM's job, not the language's.
cards/6/options/0: DTOs, messages, dictionary keys, immutable values
cards/6/options/1: EF entities with mutable state and identity
cards/6/explain: An entity with an Id is usually compared by Id, not by every field.
cards/7/pairs/1/1: Value type with the same conveniences
cards/7/pairs/3/1: Can only be set at creation
